classification.difficultyReason: Both mean and SD differ, so the student must reason that the wider curve is lower and centred further right, and scale the axis to both. It is still a sketch with no calculation.

content.prompt:
The wing spans of two species of butterfly are normally distributed. Species X has mean $40$ mm and standard deviation $3$ mm, and Species Y has mean $50$ mm and standard deviation $6$ mm.
Draw both normal curves on the same axes, marking the means.

answer.short: Sample sketch: a tall, narrow curve centred at $40$ and a shorter, wider curve centred at $50$.
answer.worked: Species Y has the larger standard deviation, so its curve is wider and lower. Species X has the smaller standard deviation, so its curve is narrower and taller. Centre X at $40$ and Y at $50$ on the same axis.
